analysis.title: "Equities Are Pricing A Slowdown, Rates Are Pricing Inflation": Goldman's Privorotsky Can't Square The Defensive Rotation
key_insights: Asia sold off hard on Monday Nov 16. The Taiex fell 6%, the Kospi 3.6% and the Nikkei 2.4%, led by semiconductor equipment and chip names. Japanese domestic consumer and healthcare names rose. Privorotsky reads the tape as AI = beta + momentum.

Privorotsky argues the market treated Nvidia's CEO departure as a tactical redistribution of hardware share. He thinks the larger question is how long the aggregate AI enterprise capex cycle lasts, and whether this is a rotation or the start of a digestion phase.

Goldman's Dominic Wilson (2027 outlook, 'Growing Pains') says AI spending should keep growing but the pace could peak early next year. AI accounts for far more of earnings growth and market value change than of GDP growth, so a spending slowdown hurts stocks more than the economy.

Nvidia reports Q3 on Tuesday. Privorotsky expects the print to be unlikely to resolve the debate on future AI commitments. It likely confirms the stock is heavily discounted on next year's numbers, but the right multiple for 2028 and beyond is unknowable. The stock is down 30% over six straight weeks.

Treasuries had a poor week. Privorotsky counts multiple-sigma moves higher in nominal yields, and all three Treasury auctions reportedly tailed. The 3Y tailed the most since May and the 10Y the most since February on weak foreign demand. PPI was tamer but did not change the selloff.

Credit held in better than equities despite the rate move. Privorotsky's reading is that reduced AI commitments are negative for equity growth expectations but positive for credit because balance sheet risk falls. The article counters that AI-related IG spreads have widened to the year's wides while non-AI IG sits near average.

Goldman prime book flows show pros trading around the AI selloff. US flows were dominated by single-stock shorting, partly offset by ETF short covering. Hedge funds net sold US equities for a second week. Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 2.6 points while the overall PB book cut gross by 2 points, mostly in Asia and Europe.

Valuation dispersion is the core puzzle. Parts of semis are near historical valuation lows while consumer staples trade at large forward-earnings premiums. Goldman's AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P, even though consensus expects 31% 2028 earnings growth. At a market multiple, current prices imply 2028 earnings falling about 6%.

Privorotsky says defensives make sense if nominal and real yields fall alongside growth, but they are not falling. Equities price a slowdown while rates price persistent inflation and restrictive policy. He asks whether receiving rates is the better expression.

Positioning is the main support. Sentiment is depressed (AAII near the low end of its range, CNN fear/greed only starting to recover). PB net exposure to global AI stocks is in the 3rd percentile of the past year and CTAs are near max short in the Nasdaq 100. Privorotsky calls it a push between challenging macro and positioning.

Goldman's derivatives desk (Brian Garrett) flags a $40 billion one-week drop in global vol-control equity exposure. Its models point to roughly $27 billion of further SPX supply over the next few sessions until volatility falls enough for these funds to re-risk.

S&P 500 earnings are a record roughly 8% of GDP on a four-quarter average, above the 1995-present trend near 6% and the 2021 peak near 7% (read off a chart, approximate). With AI supplying a large share of earnings growth, a capex digestion phase would hit index margins when bonds are not offering lower discount rates.

The article's own lean is that equities are right to price a slowdown and the bond market's inflation pricing is more likely to be wrong. It sees a squeeze as possible after a non-disastrous Nvidia print but not a sustained recovery, and suggests receiving rates is the trade that needs neither AI nor Nvidia.

Week ahead per Privorotsky: US retail sales and Home Depot Tuesday, Target, Lowe's and TJX Wednesday, Walmart Thursday (watch trade-down, margins and the defensive premium). FOMC minutes Wednesday, Fed speakers including Williams and Warsh matter given the rates repricing. UK employment and CPI, and a French Senate vote on the social security financing bill Wednesday.

tension_points.bull_case: AI spending should keep growing per Wilson, and the Nvidia stock is already heavily discounted on next year's numbers. Goldman's AI Semis basket is at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P, with consensus 2028 earnings growth of 31%.
tension_points.bear_case: Privorotsky worries the real issue is a broader digestion phase in aggregate AI capex after Huang's departure, with spending growth possibly peaking early next year. AI drives 62% of US earnings growth, so a slowdown hits equity multiples and index margins.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia's Q3 print on Tuesday Nov 17 and its commentary on future AI commitments. Privorotsky expects the print to leave the debate unresolved.

tension_points.bull_case: The defensive rotation reflects a slowdown that equities are pricing, with low vol and quality bid and beta and momentum coming down.
tension_points.bear_case: Rates are pricing persistent inflation and restrictive policy, and staples trade at enormous forward premiums. Privorotsky says defensives make sense only if nominal and real yields fall alongside growth, and they are not.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nominal and real yields falling alongside growth would validate the defensive rotation. This week's retail earnings (Home Depot, Target, Lowe's, TJX, Walmart) test whether the defensive premium is justified.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is washed out, with PB net exposure in the 3rd percentile, CTAs near max short in the Nasdaq 100 and depressed sentiment. Privorotsky thinks this drove last week's squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: With AI leadership under pressure, expensive defensives and little relief from rates, it is hard to identify what drives a sustained recovery. Vol-control funds may sell about $27 billion more SPX.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Volatility falling enough for vol-control funds to re-risk would end the systematic supply, per the desk's models.
